SURGERY (GENERAL)__Intestinal Ischaemia:
Mesenteric Blood Supply

Three main branches of abdominal aorta: Coeliac artery (foregut: stomach → duodenum), Superior mesenteric artery / SMA (midgut: small bowel → splenic flexure), Inferior mesenteric artery / IMA (hindgut: left colon → rectum). Collateral supply means at least 2 vessels must be compromised for chronic symptoms.

Chronic Mesenteric Ischaemia — Intestinal Angina

Atherosclerosis narrows mesenteric vessels → postprandial pain (intestines cannot meet demand after eating).

Classic Triad
  • Postprandial central colicky abdominal pain — onset 30 min after eating, lasts 1–2 hours
  • Weight loss (food avoidance + malabsorption)
  • Abdominal bruits on auscultation
Management
  • Modify CVD risk factors (statin, antiplatelet, stop smoking)
  • Revascularisation — ENDOVASCULAR first-line: percutaneous mesenteric angioplasty ± stenting
  • Open surgery (endarterectomy, bypass grafting) if endovascular fails or unsuitable
Acute Mesenteric Ischaemia

Surgical emergency. Sudden occlusion of SMA (usually embolus from AF or thrombosis). Bowel necrosis develops rapidly.

🏃
Key Risk Factor
AF (most common) → LAA thrombus embolises → lodges in SMA
😣
Pain
Acute severe central abdominal pain — OUT OF PROPORTION to clinical examination findings
🤢
Associated Symptoms
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea (bloody in late disease)
😰
Systemic
Shock, peritonitis, sepsis as bowel becomes necrotic
Investigations
🩻
CT Angiography
Gold standard — shows occlusion, bowel wall thickening, pneumatosis intestinalis (gas in bowel wall = necrosis)
🧪
ABG
Metabolic acidosis + raised lactate — from ischaemic bowel (lactic acid production)
🔬
Bloods
FBC, U&E, clotting, amylase, LFTs — usually non-specific initially
Management
💉
IV ResuscitationFluids, analgesia (IV opioids), NBM
↓
💊
Broad-Spectrum AntibioticsBowel may perforate → risk of faecal peritonitis
↓
🏥
Emergency SurgeryTwo objectives: (1) Remove necrotic bowel (2) Revascularise — embolectomy/bypass ± thrombolysis
↓
🔄
Second-Look Laparotomy24–48h later to reassess bowel viability — further resection if needed
⭐ Exam Pearls
Acute mesenteric ischaemia: pain OUT OF PROPORTION to clinical findings = classic presentation. Think of it in any AF patient with acute abdomen.
Metabolic acidosis + raised lactate = bowel ischaemia until proven otherwise. Emergency CT angiography.
Pneumatosis intestinalis (gas in bowel wall on CT) = bowel has full-thickness infarction → imminent perforation. Emergency theatre.
Chronic mesenteric ischaemia triad: postprandial pain + weight loss + abdominal bruits. Need ≥2 vessels compromised (collateral supply).
Endovascular (angioplasty/stenting) is first-line for chronic mesenteric ischaemia — less invasive than open surgery.
